scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: Siguiendo el Music for Films de Eno, música para películas que solo existen en la imaginación: Barry Adamson (ex Magazine y Bad Seeds), pionero en sustituir la orquesta por el sampler; David Holmes, entre Carpenter y Morricone, acabó componiendo para Soderbergh; Red Snapper, Craig Armstrong, In the Nursery. John Barry, compositor icono del trip-hop.
scenes.family: Hip hop, breaks y ritmo lento

podcast.title: Departure from Bond Films
podcast.body: John Barry had moved on from scoring Bond films by 1989, making "Licensed to Kill" the first title song not to involve him. His extensive contributions to the franchise had defined much of its musical character for decades. "He had moved on from scoring Bond films."

xref.title: Early Practice Locations
xref.body: Adam Yauch's letter at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction mentioned early band practices taking place at John Barry's loft on 100th Street and Broadway, where John's father would interrupt them, and also at Adam Yauch's home in Brooklyn during hot summer days, with windows open, disturbing the neighborhood. "To Keith Sheldonbach, to John Barry, to John Barry's loft on a hundredth street and Broadway, where John's dead would come busting in during our first practice as screaming when you turn that f*** off already."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: John Berry's Departure
xref.body: Guitarist John Berry quit the band near the end of 1982, reportedly due to a "meth problem." "John Barry quit near the end of 1982, apparently there was a bit of a meth problem."
